title: Send a written meeting summary within four hours
why_matters: Writing the summary forces you to decide what mattered. Sending it within four hours means the writing is honest — you can't yet remember everything in soft focus, and you have to commit. The BAs who do this build a reputation for being the person who keeps decisions visible. That reputation compounds.
steps: Pick a meeting you attended this week with at least three people and at least one decision.
Within four hours of the meeting ending, write three short sections: what was decided, what's open, what's the next action and who owns it.
Keep it to one screen. If it's longer, you're including narrative; cut.
Send it to everyone who was in the meeting. Add the meeting's name and date in the subject line.
success_criteria: The summary email is sent within four hours of the meeting. It contains decisions, opens, and an owner per action. At least one person replies with a correction (this is good; absence of correction means nobody read it).
reflection_prompt: What got cut between your draft and what you sent, and was the cut a discipline or a duck?
